title: Concurrent stream limit for playback sessions
name: Playback session limiter

defect.snippet: await client.query("BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED");

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces the per-account stream limit when several devices start playback at once? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: start() counts active sessions and then inserts a new one, but runs under READ COMMITTED with no lock on the account. Two devices starting at the same moment both count, say, 1 of 2, neither sees the other's uncommitted insert, and both insert, leaving 3 active streams on a 2-stream plan. This is write skew; it needs SERIALIZABLE (with retry on 40001) or a lock that serializes starts per account, e.g. SELECT ... FROM accounts WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE before counting.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A phone crashes without calling stop(), then the same phone starts a new stream two minutes later. How does its old session affect the limit check?
choices: It counts as active until a cleanup job removes it
It is deleted by the device_id DELETE before counting, so it does not count
It causes a 410 on the new start request
It counts only if its title_id matches the new title
choiceQuestions.explanation: Before counting, start() deletes any session for the same account and device, so the stale session is gone. (It would also be excluded by the 90 second heartbeat filter.) There is no cleanup job in this code, 410 is only returned by heartbeat, and title_id plays no part in the count.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The INSERT into playback_sessions fails with a constraint error. What state is left behind?
choices: The device's previous session stays deleted while the new one is missing
The DELETE and the failed INSERT are both rolled back, so the previous session is restored
The connection is returned to the pool with the transaction still open
The client receives a 409 stream_limit response
choiceQuestions.explanation: The DELETE and INSERT run on the same client inside BEGIN/COMMIT; the catch runs ROLLBACK, undoing the delete too. The finally block releases the client only after rollback, and only ConcurrentStreamLimitError maps to 409; other errors go to next().

choiceQuestions.prompt: An account on a 2-stream plan has 2 sessions whose last heartbeat was 5 minutes ago, on other devices. A third device calls start(). What happens?
choices: 409 stream_limit, because the two rows still exist
The stale rows are deleted and then the new session is created
A new session is created; the stale rows are ignored by the count but not deleted
The request fails because the plan lookup returns no rows
choiceQuestions.explanation: The count filters on last_heartbeat within 90 seconds, so stale rows are not counted, and the DELETE only removes rows for the calling device. The rows remain but do not block the new session. The plan lookup succeeds for an existing account.
